values: Materials and setup | All data are fictional and editorially designed

A1 | A fictional customer has a cotton canvas bag with about 6 cm of opened side seam; the request is only to restore the side seam, without changing the handles, zipper, or bag shape. Delivery is required on 2026-09-23.

A2 | Matching-color thread, hand sewing needles, scissors, a ruler, and clips are available. The original side seam allowance is about 1 cm; materials and dates are exercise inputs only, not market quotations.

A3 | Define acceptance criteria beforehand: the repair covers the 6 cm opened seam, with 1 cm of reinforcement at each end; target stitch spacing is no greater than 5 mm, thread ends are secured, and the bag surface shows no obvious loosening; another person checks these four items individually.

A4 | Inspection reveals another 2 cm of worn fabric edge beyond the end of the opened seam; sewing directly along the original line may cause it to split again. The original requirements do not approve patches or appearance changes.

A5 | First record the damage, test sew without touching the customer's property, and propose a reinforcement plan; obtain customer confirmation before any actual repair that changes the bag's appearance or adds materials.
Scope of materials | A1–A5 are fictional exercises; do not present the exercise acceptance conditions as universal industry standards.
Task | Write a repair plan and checklist
Using A1–A5, list materials, markings, stitch choices, reinforcement, and the acceptance sequence, identifying matters requiring additional confirmation after the expanded wear is discovered.
Deliverables | A written plan, a scrap-fabric test sewing sample, and before-and-after repair records; handling actual customer property is not required.
Reference answer | Check boundaries first

A1/A3: 6+1+1=8 cm is the originally planned stitching extent, rather than sewing only 6 cm; A4 does not establish the location of the additional 2 cm of wear or the reinforcement plan, so you cannot directly infer a final extent of 10 cm or claim the original 8 cm will necessarily be strong.

Test sew on scrap fabric and check stitch spacing, reinforcement, and thread ends against A3; first mark wear on the actual bag and ask whether reinforcement or appearance changes are acceptable, without continuing any plan that may change appearance before confirmation.

The handoff record states the original requirements in A1, the new finding in A4, the reinforcement method awaiting confirmation, and delivery time; only after consent should you sew to updated requirements and review each item.

Stitch spacing and reinforcement extent are settings for this exercise, not safety certification or employer standards. Without customer confirmation, do not conceal wear, change appearance, or state "accepted."
